```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

hovercraft puts a tip on any HTML tag in a Shiny app or a bslib page. The tip shows when the pointer rests on the tag or
keyboard focus arrives on it, and hides when either leaves. It is plain text, or drawn from a template and filled in from
the values of one item, such as a row of a table.

```{r}
library(hovercraft)
```

## A tip with text

`tip_on()` takes a tag and the text. The text is markdown (strong, emphasis, code, links and short lists), shown as
written: build it with `paste0()` or `sprintf()` when it holds values.

```{r}
run <- tip_on(htmltools::tags$button("Run"), "Runs the **check**")
run
```

The tag comes back with the tip's attributes and the engine's script and CSS attached, so it works wherever you put it:
in a bslib page, in a plain Shiny page and in output made later with `renderUI()`.

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "48%", fig.alt = "A button labelled Run, with a dark tip below it that reads: Runs the check.", fig.show = "hold"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("figures/default-light.png", "figures/default-dark.png"))
```

The tip follows the page. On a page with a `bslib::bs_theme()` it uses the theme's colours and turns dark with
`bslib::input_dark_mode()`. See `vignette("themes")` to set its look yourself.

## A tip from a template

When many tags show the same kind of tip, write the tip once as a template and give each tag its values.

```{r}
tip_define(
  diff = tip_template(
    tip_title("{{ label }}"),
    tip_badge("{{ status }}"),
    tip_fields(Records = "{{ records | number:0 }}", Differences = "{{ differences | number:0 }}"),
    tip_text("{{ share | percent:1 }} of the records differ.")
  )
)
```

`tip_define()` returns tags: put it once in the page's UI. A template is a list of blocks, shown in order:

| Block | Shows |
|---|---|
| `tip_title()` | the first line |
| `tip_text()` | a paragraph of markdown |
| `tip_badge()` | a short label |
| `tip_fields()` | label and value pairs |
| `tip_code()` | code, as text |

A placeholder is `{{ field }}`, or `{{ field | number:2 }}` and `{{ field | percent:1 }}` to round. It names one field of the
record, exactly, and a value that is missing or blank shows a dash. A mistake in a placeholder, such as one that never
closes, stops with an error when the template is made, not later in the browser.

Then name the template and give the tag a record, a named list of single values or a data frame of one row:

```{r}
row <- list(label = "ADAE", status = "Check", records = 5304, differences = 3, share = 0.0006)
tip_on(htmltools::tags$button("ADAE"), template = "diff", record = row)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "48%", fig.alt = "A button labelled ADAE, with a tip below it holding a title, a badge, two label and value pairs and a sentence.", fig.show = "hold"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("figures/template-light.png", "figures/template-dark.png"))
```

## A tip on every row of a table

`tip_rows()` turns a data frame into one record per row. Name the columns the template uses, so nothing else in the data is
written into the page:

```{r}
files <- data.frame(
  label = c("ADAE", "ADSL"),
  status = c("Check", "Same"),
  records = c(5304, 306),
  differences = c(3, 0),
  share = c(0.0006, 0),
  reviewer = c("A. Reviewer", "B. Reviewer")
)
records <- tip_rows(files, columns = c("label", "status", "records", "differences", "share"))
rows <- lapply(records, function(record) {
  tip_on(
    htmltools::tags$tr(htmltools::tags$td(record$label), tabindex = "0"),
    template = "diff",
    record = record
  )
})
length(rows)
```

Once `tip_define()` has seen a template, `tip_on()` keeps only the columns it names, so a record that holds more is not
written out in full. A record that holds a value a tip cannot show, such as a list or a data frame, is an error that says which.

## Keyboard users

A tip shows on keyboard focus, so a tag that cannot take focus, such as a table row or a `div`, gives a keyboard user no
way to its tip. `tip_on()` says so once. It never adds a tab stop itself, because a table of 3,000 rows would become
3,000 Tab stops: give the tags worth a stop `tabindex = "0"`, as above, or put the tip on a button or a link.

## In a Shiny app

```r
library(shiny)
library(hovercraft)

ui <- bslib::page_fluid(
  tip_define(hint = tip_template(tip_title("{{ label }}"), tip_text("{{ n }} files"))),
  uiOutput("buttons")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$buttons <- renderUI({
    tip_on(actionButton("go", "Go"), template = "hint", record = list(label = "Go", n = 3))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

A template belongs to the whole page. A Shiny module should put its id in the names it defines, such as
`paste0(id, "_row")`, so two modules do not replace each other's templates.
